title: AEGS Agent Identity (Know Your Agent)
description: What an ecosystem participant may need to know about an autonomous economic actor. Deliberately pseudonymous at its core: `agentId` is a stable handle, not a person. Everything that could identify a human or an organisation is optional, separately grouped, and excluded from counterparty disclosure by default -- because a standard that makes real-world identity the price of transacting has answered the accountability question by abolishing privacy.

agentId.description: A stable pseudonymous handle. AEGS does not require it to resolve to a legal person; whether it must is a deployment and jurisdiction question, not a protocol one.

purpose.description: What this agent exists to do. Distinct from an Economic Intent, which is what it was sent to do on one occasion.

status.description: `suspended` is reversible, `revoked` is terminal. Both stop the agent transacting; keeping them distinct lets an operator pause an agent without destroying the record of it having been authorised.

parentAgentId.description: The agent that delegated authority to this one. A sub-agent's authority can never exceed its parent's -- a delegation that widens authority is an escalation, and AEGS requires implementations to refuse it.

controller.description: PRIVATE. The party that controls this agent's keys. Excluded from counterparty disclosure by default.

operator.description: PRIVATE. The party accountable for what this agent does, where that differs from the controller.

wallets.description: PRIVATE by default. A counterparty already sees the address that pays it; publishing the full set links an agent's activity across counterparties, which is a surveillance surface rather than a control.

authorizedNetworks.description: Settlement networks this agent may transact on, as CAIP-2 identifiers. An empty list means unrestricted.

spendingLimits.description: PRIVATE. What the controller asserts this agent may spend. An implementation applies this as an ADDITIONAL constraint -- the narrower of this and its own policy -- never as a widening. Never disclosed to a counterparty: telling a seller the remaining budget invites it to charge exactly that.

credentials.description: References to credentials held elsewhere -- a DID document, a verifiable credential, an attestation. AEGS 0.1 defines the reference, NOT verification: an implementation that lists a credential is not thereby claiming to have checked it, and `verified` says which.

verified.description: False means listed but unchecked. AEGS 0.1 has no verification mechanism, so an honest implementation reports false here rather than implying assurance it has not obtained.

riskProfile.description: A deployment's own classification of this agent. AEGS does not define the vocabulary; it requires only that the value be recorded rather than inferred.

policyVersion.description: The governance policy in force when this identity was registered, as a content hash.
